units.text: Reserve the slot as a capped $0.6M option, bridge 2028 with the contract molder, and order the line only once signed demand and funding clear set triggers
The gap is real and starts in 2028, but its size hinges on unsigned demand
Measured on accepted units, the line is 92% utilized in 2027, not 83%; overflow starts in 2028 (0.6M units)
At forecast, overflow reaches 3.5M units by 2030. At signed minimums it is only 0.9M
Of the 12.4M units forecast for 2030, 2.6M (21%) sit above signed minimums and are nonbinding (2.6M of 2030 volume is unsigned)
The 98% fill rate is measured monthly, for every medical-device customer; missing it twice gives the customer the right to rebid its whole supplier allocation, not just the units missed
Ordering now breaks the cash covenant; doing nothing breaks the fill-rate standard
A full order leaves $4.0M of cash against the $7.0M floor ($3.0M short), and no borrowing facility exists: $11.0M - $2.2M committed R&D - $4.8M = $4.0M
Doing nothing leaves 0.6M units unserved at the 2028 peak and 3.5M by 2030
The molder covers 2028-29 for $0.07-0.27M a year (a cheap bridge through 2029), but at forecast it falls 1.0M units short in 2030 and cannot make the specialty product

The slot is a capped option worth buying, provided the order date can move: pay the deposit as insurance, on condition that its order date can be deferred. Without that, the insurance lapses before funding arrives
With the deposit paid, $8.8M - $0.6M = $8.2M, still $1.2M above the $7.0M floor; the most we can lose is the (forfeited) $0.6M deposit

The slot pays for itself only by protecting customer allocations (only if it heads off an allocation rebid). On incremental margin alone it does not; on lost units alone, the deposit would not be worth paying
As offered, the slot expects an order by June 2027, but funding is only plausible in 2028. Agree a later order date before paying
Three hard triggers turn the reservation into a full order: release the $4.2M balance only when all three triggers are met: demand, funding and readiness
Demand trigger: signed 2029 or 2030 minimums of 10.5M units or more (today 9.4M / 9.8M), including take-or-pay or prepaid volume
OR (alternative demand trigger): the monthly simulation shows 2+ months below 98% with the molder at its contracted capacity (a simulated fill-rate breach in 2+ months)
Funding trigger: at least $3.5M of committed funding, so cash after the $4.2M payment is $7.5M or more. Arithmetic: $8.2M - $4.2M = $4.0M; plus $3.5M = $7.5M, i.e. the $7.0M floor plus a $0.5M buffer
Readiness trigger: supplier confirms installation within 12 months of order at a fixed price; specialty validation plan in place (supplier dates and the specialty validation plan confirmed)
Target decision Q1 2028, last possible date Q3 2028
Cash figures exclude 2027-30 operating cash flow, which the pack does not give; cash tests use commitments against $8.8M. Positive cash flow would ease the funding trigger

The starting hypothesis (reserve now, gate the order) survives the tests, but only with a funding plan and a flexible order date. Starting hypothesis = Operations Director's proposal: reserve the slot, release the machine only after signed orders and a liquidity review
H1 'A full order now does not fit within the covenant': Holds
H2 '2028 overflow can be served without the new line': Holds. 0.6M units of overflow vs the molder's 2.5M ceiling; 5 months' notice needed; specialty volume not yet in 2028

H3 'Demand beyond the molder's reach is credible within the line's lead time': Partly. At forecast, 2030 overflow is 3.5M (1.0M over the ceiling). At signed minimums it is 0.9M. Two programs slipped a quarter last year
H4 'The slot is affordable and its downside is capped': Holds
H5 'The $4.2M balance can be funded when the order must be placed': Not yet. No committed facility. The prepayment / signed-volume loan is uncontracted and the CFO sees it in 2028

H6 'The slot secures timing we could not get without it': Unverified. The slot reserves an installation crew, not capacity. The pack gives no lead time without a slot; its timeline assumes an order by June 2027
Revision: same direction, tighter conditions. H5 becomes a release trigger; H6 must be settled with the supplier before the March deposit
The '17% free capacity' view divides by nameplate output: the Ops KPI divides units started by nameplate hours and reports quality rejects separately, so it overstates headroom

Forecast good units 8.3 / 9.6 / 11.2 / 12.4 M (2027-2030) vs Nameplate 10.0M and Practical 9.0M; practical accepted capacity of 9.0M units is net of maintenance, validated changeovers and quality holds
Real 2027 slack is 0.7M units (7.8%), not 1.7M (17%)

Specialty runs scrap 4 points more than the standard mix, and the forecast has no allowance for it: about 0.09-0.10M units of capacity lost a year from 2029. Calculation: 20% x 11.2M = 2.24M specialty units x 4% = 0.09M (2030: 2.48M x 4% = 0.10M)
The plant has no real buffer for 2028 peaks: whatever the decision, the bridge has to be in place before the 2028 peak

Overflow above internal capacity, millions of accepted units (2028 / 2029 / 2030): Forecast 0.6 / 2.3 / 3.5; Forecast slips one year 0 / 0.7 / 2.3; Signed minimums only 0 / 0.5 / 0.9; Molder ceiling 2.5M
Timing: two key design programs slipped a quarter last year; a one-year slip pushes the molder ceiling breach from 2030 to 2031

Overflow = demand above 9.0M practical capacity plus the specialty scrap allowance (20% of 2029-30 units x 4%); specialty volume adds roughly 0.1M units of overflow a year through extra scrap. Forecast overflow = 0.6 / 2.29 / 3.50M (2028-30)
Only the forecast case needs a second line before 2031. Committing $4.8M before customers sign is a bet on the top bar
The new line is needed only if unsigned demand arrives on time, so signed volume should trigger the order
Downside cases: Slip case = forecast delayed one year (assumption); weak case = signed minimums. Other paths fall between these
Annual totals understate the risk: the 98% standard is measured monthly, and with the molder maxed out, 2029 runs at 98% of monthly supply
Internal practical rate is ~0.75M units a month; the molder adds at most ~0.21M a month
Several customer launches inside one six-week window can exceed the monthly rate even when the year fits (plant supervisor)
Molder limits: five months' notice; holiday-period capacity not yet committed
Base business of 9.0M units x $0.45 = ~$4.0M of annual contribution exposed to a rebid (proxy)
Losing a quarter of it costs ~$1.0M a year, more than the $0.45M lost on the 2030 forecast shortfall itself
A monthly simulation or an inventory buffer is needed to confirm compliance

Average month at forecast (M units), 2028 / 2029 / 2030: demand (annual forecast / 12) 0.80 / 0.93 / 1.03; max supply, internal (after scrap) + molder (2.5M / 12): 0.75 + 0.21 = 0.96 / 0.74 + 0.21 = 0.95 / 0.74 + 0.21 = 0.95
Demand as % of max monthly supply: 83% / 98% / 109% (2028 / 2029 / 2030); how far a peak month can exceed the average: ~20% / ~2% / None: short every month
In 2029 even the molder bridge leaves only ~2% monthly headroom: a launch cluster could trigger the two misses that open a rebid
Monthly rates = annual capacity / 12 (even-flow simplification). Contribution proxy uses the pack's $0.45/unit for serving rather than refusing demand

Cash after 2027 commitments, $M: Do nothing $8.8M; Molder only $8.8M; Reserve slot $8.2M; Order line now $4.0M; Floor $7.0M. Cash test: Order now 11.0 - 2.2 - 4.8 = 4.0 (headroom -3.0); Reserve slot 11.0 - 2.2 - 0.6 = 8.2 (headroom +1.2)

The Sales VP's '23% faster growth' claim compares companies at one point in time: the early builders also held more advance purchase commitments and sold into faster-growing therapeutic segments. It cannot show that building capacity caused the growth (does not show cause and effect)
The board will not accept 'demand is growing' as a reason to breach the floor
With no facility, ordering in 2027 needs at least $3.0M of new funding. 'Order now' is ruled out on cash
Only 'reserve the slot + molder bridge' passes every hard constraint while keeping 2030 capacity available

Order line now: 2027 covenant Fails: $4.0M; 2028 service: Line from ~Jan 2028; 2030 at forecast: Covered; Specialty: In-house; 2027-30 cost at forecast $6.45M = 4.8 + 3 x 0.55; Reversibility: $4.8M sunk

Reserve slot + molder bridge (recommended): 2027 covenant Passes: $8.2M; 2028 service: Molder, $0.07M; 2030 at forecast: Covered if triggers met by Q3 2028; Specialty: In-house priority; cost $5.8M if ordered Q1 2028; $0.6M + premium if not; Reversibility: Max loss $0.6M

Molder only: 2027 covenant Passes: $8.8M; 2028 service: Molder, $0.07M; 2030 at forecast: 1.0M units short; Specialty: Molder not validated; cost $0.65M premium + $0.45M lost (2030) + rebid risk; Fully flexible
Do nothing: 2027 covenant Passes: $8.8M; 2028: 0.6M unserved; 2030 at forecast: 3.5M unserved; cost $2.9M lost contribution + rebid risk

How the recommended path's $5.8M builds up: $4.8M line (deposit credited, not double-counted) + $0.07M molder premium in 2028 + $0.14M for H1 2029 + $0.83M fixed cost for mid-2029 to 2030 (0.55 x 1.5 years). That is $0.6M less than ordering now ($6.45M), because fixed costs start about 18 months later
Molder only is cheapest to 2029 but cannot meet forecast 2030 demand. Do nothing fails in the first peak
Choosing 'reserve + bridge' over 'order now' costs nothing in capacity; it removes the covenant breach and a $4.8M bet on unsigned demand
units.correct_version: Choosing 'reserve + bridge' over 'order now' removes the covenant breach and a $4.8M bet on unsigned demand, but it does give up capacity headroom: under the recommended path the line produces from about mid-2029 rather than about January 2028, so 2028 and early 2029 run on the molder bridge, which leaves only ~2% monthly headroom in 2029.

units.text: Costs are 2027-30 incremental cash at forecast demand: capex, $0.55M/yr fixed cost from commissioning, molder premium $0.12/unit, lost contribution $0.45/unit. They exclude operating cash flow and value after 2030
Use the molder to bridge 2028-29. It is not a substitute for the line if forecast 2030 demand arrives
Molder economics (2028 / 2029 / 2030): units sent to molder 0.6 / 2.29 / 2.5 (cap) M; premium @ $0.12: $0.07M / $0.27M / $0.30M; unserved units 0 / 0 / 1.0M; lost contribution @ $0.45: 0 / 0 / $0.45M

Forecast overflow (incl. specialty scrap) vs ceiling 2.5M: 2028 0.6M = 24% of ceiling; 2029 2.3M = 92% of ceiling; 2030 3.5M = 140%: 1.0M short. 2029 at 92% of the ceiling leaves 0.2M units of annual slack
Specialty (20% of 2029 units, 2.24M) is not validated at the molder, so it must run in-house and takes the internal slack
Still worth using: serving through the molder keeps $0.33 of the $0.45 unit contribution, against $0 for a refused order
Premium of $0.12/accepted unit excludes first-article validation for the specialty product

The new line is insurance for customer allocations, not a margin play: it beats the molder on running cost only above 4.6M overflow units a year (= $0.55M line fixed cost / $0.12 molder premium per unit)
Forecast overflow peaks at 3.5M (2030), so within the molder's 2.5M ceiling, buying is cheaper than running a second line, even before the $4.8M capex
The line saves $0.12 per unit inside the ceiling, but $0.45 per unit beyond it

2030 at forecast ($M/yr): New line serves 3.5M internally, contribution 3.5 x 0.45 = 1.58, line fixed cost -0.55, net before $4.8M capex 1.03, 0 unserved; Molder only serves 2.5M via molder, 2.5 x 0.33 = 0.83, fixed cost 0, net 0.83, 1.0M left unserved (rebid trigger). So the line earns only ~$0.20M a year more than the molder in 2030

The $4.8M is justified by what it protects: fill-rate compliance in peak months, which protects ~$4.0M a year of base contribution from rebids; in-house capacity for the specialty product the molder cannot make; growth after 2030: each 1M units above the molder ceiling adds $0.45M a year to the line's advantage
Because the case rests on protecting allocations, the order trigger should be signed customer volume, not forecast margin
No salvage value, useful life or discount rate is given, so the comparison is on annual running economics only. $0.45 and $0.12 are not compared as if they were alternative price quotes
What happens to the $0.6M: Line ordered (triggers met): credited toward the $4.8M, net cost of the slot $0. Line not ordered: forfeited, net cost $0.6M
Scale check (signed-minimum case): the $0.6M equals ~5.5 years of the 2030 molder premium ($0.11M)

Loss avoided if 2030 capacity is late by one year, and break-even probability: shortfall only, 1.0M units x $0.45 = $0.45M, 133%: not justified; + rebid loses 25% of base allocation = $1.46M, 41%; + rebid loses 50% of base allocation = $2.48M, 24%
The deposit uses a third of the $1.8M headroom ($11.0M - $2.2M = $8.8M available above commitments), leaving room for 2028-29 molder premiums ($0.35M)
The deposit does not fund the line: the $4.2M balance still needs at least $3.0M of new money ($8.8M - $0.6M = $8.2M; - $4.2M balance = $4.0M, deposit not double-counted)
It is worth paying if there is roughly a 1-in-4 to 2-in-5 chance that the slot is what keeps a customer's allocation. Today's 2.6M of unsigned 2030 volume and the 2028 overflow make that plausible
That chance is only real if the slot buys timing we could not otherwise get (H6)

Break-even probability = $0.6M at risk / loss avoided for one year of late capacity. Rebid shares (25% / 50%) are illustrative, applied to the 9.0M-unit base x $0.45 proxy; changes break-even, not direction
Reserving the slot becomes a bad option under five conditions; the two most likely can be tested before the March deposit

Condition 1: The order must be placed by June 2027, while funding is only plausible in 2028. We would have to forfeit $0.6M or breach the covenant. Negotiate an order date of Q1 2028 or later (install H1 2029); otherwise decline. Before Mar 2027

Condition 2: The slot buys nothing scarce: a 12-month lead time is available without it. Paying $0.6M for timing we would get anyway. Get written lead time and crew availability without a slot. Before Mar 2027
Condition 3: Demand stays near signed minimums. Overflow of 0.9M or less through 2030; molder covers it for $0.11M a year or less. Track signed volume quarterly; kill at the go/no-go gate. Gate 2
Condition 4: Programs slip a year. The line arrives a year early and carries $0.55M a year of fixed cost before it is needed. Use the deferral right; molder covers 2030 at 92% of its ceiling. Gate 2
Condition 5: Cash headroom erodes in 2027. The deposit uses $0.6M of $1.8M headroom; pre-build stock and validation compete for the rest. 13-week cash forecast; cap pre-build working capital. Monthly
If the supplier will not move the order date to Q1 2028 or later, decline the slot and plan on the molder plus a 2028 order at standard lead time, once that lead time is confirmed

The pack gives no slot expiry or deferral terms; the June 2027 order date comes from the stated 'if ordered by June 2027, machine expected mid-2028'. Assume an order by June 2027 unless renegotiated; made a condition of the deposit. If deferral is already allowed, the case for the slot gets stronger
Cover 2028 in three layers: the contract molder booked by June 2027, a 2027 safety stock, and specialty kept in-house
Book 0.6M units for 2028 (24% of the ceiling), about $0.07M of premium
Formal notice is 5 months, but sign by 30 June 2027 to lock in holiday-period capacity
Hold an option on up to 2.3M units for 2029 (~$0.27M)
Get a quote and timeline for specialty first-article validation as a hedge
2027 has 0.7M units of practical slack (9.0M - 8.3M), more than the 2028 overflow: pre-build standard containers ahead of the 2028 peak to absorb launch clustering
Safety stock depends on shelf-life and customer lot rules; cap the working capital so cash headroom holds
Schedule specialty first on the own line; the molder is not validated for it
Add a 4-point specialty scrap allowance to the plan (~0.1M units a year)
Run a monthly fill-rate simulation (launch windows, holidays, scrap) by Q2 2027

2028 coverage check (M units): contract molder 2.5 available, planned use 0.6 (24%), $0.07M premium; 2027 safety stock from practical slack up to 0.7, peak-month buffer, working capital (unit cost not in pack); total cover 3.2 vs 0.6M forecast overflow, ~5x the overflow; fixed capex $0
Only a January 2027 order, which breaches the covenant, gets the line in before the 2028 peak; any compliant order arrives after it, so 2028 needs this bridge
The pack says the 2028 peak starts before mid-2028; we assume around Q2 2028, so the latest molder notice is about November 2027. An earlier peak brings the molder notice date forward
Why 10.5M: signed overflow (~1.6M) would already use two-thirds of the molder ceiling, and fewer than half of the remaining 1.9M unsigned forecast units would exhaust it
Funding sources: customer prepayment, or a supplemental loan backed by a signed-volume guarantee; pricing to be negotiated
Readiness detail: plan allows +2 months for specialty validation; molder bridge contracted through commissioning; construction inflation re-quoted
Not triggers: 'demand is growing', nonbinding forecasts, peer growth statistics, or a wish to announce capacity publicly
One customer contract can meet two triggers at once: a signed-volume guarantee raises committed demand and secures the loan
10.5M threshold and $0.5M buffer are our proposals: policy choices; the committee may tighten or relax them
Internal capacity after specialty scrap ~8.9M + molder 2.5M = ~11.4M of demand coverable without the line
Four decision gates separate the provisional reservation from the full investment (Gate 0, Gate 0b, Gate 1, Gate 2, Gate 3)
Gate 0, Jan 2027 IC. Owner: CEO / IC. Approve the $0.6M deposit, conditional on supplier terms; start the molder RFQ and funding workstream; no full order, no public announcement
Gate 0b, Feb-Mar 2027. Owner: Procurement / Ops. Supplier confirms an order date of Q1 2028 or later and the lead time in writing; pay the deposit in March, or decline if terms fail

Gate 1, by Jun 2027. Owner: Operations. Molder signed for 2028, including the holiday period; monthly simulation complete; early order only if all 3 triggers are met. If ordered here: line producing ~mid-2028, after the 2028 peak starts

Gate 2, Q1 2028 (target). Owner: IC (CFO case). Go/no-go on the $4.2M balance. Go: line producing by about mid-2029 and relieves the 2029 peak. No-go: book 2029 molder volume. If ordered here: producing ~Q1-Q2 2029 (+2 months validation)

Gate 3, Q3 2028 (last date). Owner: IC. Last order date for a line producing before 2030. No-go: forfeit $0.6M, extend the molder, re-gate for 2031. If ordered here: producing ~Q3-Q4 2029, just before 2030

Line timing = 12-month lead time + commissioning; the specialty product may need 2 more months of validation (12 months from order + up to 2 months extra). Order by Q3 2028 to be producing before the 2030 peak
Provisional (Gates 0-1): $0.6M at risk, cash at or above $8.2M | Full investment (Gates 2-3): $4.2M, only with at least $3.5M committed funding
Each gate has a date, a proposed owner and a default: if a trigger is missed, the default is the cheaper, reversible path
If customer orders fall short, the plan degrades gracefully: in the weak-demand cases the worst outcome is a $0.6M forfeited deposit, never a covenant breach

Case 'Forecast, funded' (0.6 / 2.3 / 3.5 overflow): molder alone enough? No: 1.0M short in 2030. Gate outcome: triggers met: order Q1 2028. Incremental cost 2027-30: ~$5.8M incl. line. Funded case assumes $3.5M committed at Gate 2
Case 'Forecast, funded': lowest cash vs $7.0M floor = $7.5M (+0.5)
units.correct_version: Using the method applied to the other rows (deducting molder premiums from cash), the low is about $7.3M ($7.5M - $0.07M - $0.14M), i.e. about +0.3 vs the floor; deducting the line's $0.83M fixed cost to 2030 as well gives about $6.5M, below the $7.0M floor unless operating cash flow covers it.

units.text: Case 'One-year slip' (0 / 0.7 / 2.3): molder alone enough? Yes: 92% of ceiling in 2030. Gate outcome: defer the slot; re-gate for 2031. Cost: $0.36M premium (+$0.6M if no deferral). Lowest cash ~$7.8M (+0.8): $8.8M - $0.6M - $0.36M = ~$7.8M

Case 'Signed minimums only' (0 / 0.5 / 0.9): molder alone enough? Yes: 36% of ceiling or less. Gate outcome: kill at Gate 2; forfeit deposit. Cost: $0.6M + $0.16M premium. Lowest cash ~$8.0M (+1.0): $8.8M - $0.6M deposit - $0.16M premiums = ~$8.0M

Case 'Forecast demand, no funding' (0.6 / 2.3 / 3.5): molder alone enough? No: 1.0M short in 2030. Gate outcome: no order (the floor holds); molder to cap, safety stock, ration. Cost: $0.6M + $0.65M premium + $0.45M lost + rebid risk. Lowest cash ~$7.6M (+0.6): $8.8M - $0.6M - $0.65M = ~$7.6M

The case to watch is the last one: demand arrives but funding does not. The board's rule (no breach of the floor) then means accepting 2030 rebid risk. The mitigation is to make customer co-funding (prepayment or a volume guarantee) the price of guaranteed capacity, starting in 2027 negotiations
The cash floor holds in every case
units.correct_version: The cash floor holds in the three cases where no order is placed (~$7.8M, ~$8.0M, ~$7.6M). In the funded forecast case the low is about $7.3M after molder premiums, and about $6.5M once the line's $0.83M fixed cost to 2030 is also deducted, which is below the $7.0M floor unless operating cash flow covers it.

units.text: Weak demand costs at most $0.6M; the unfunded forecast case is a customer-retention risk, not a cash risk
Cash lows exclude operating cash flow. Premiums at $0.12/unit; lost contribution at $0.45/unit
The answer is most sensitive to unsigned demand timing, funding and the slot's terms; each is covered by a gate or a test before the deposit

Uncertainty: demand above signed minimums (2.6M units in 2030) and program slips. Effect: decides whether the line is needed before 2031. Handling: demand trigger on signed volume; quarterly tracking; Gate 3 last date

Uncertainty: funding: prepayment / guarantee not contracted; debt pricing not negotiated. Effect: without it, no order can be placed. Handling: funding trigger of $3.5M or more; CFO term sheet by Gate 2
Uncertainty: slot terms: order date, deferral, lead time without a slot (not in pack). Effect: decides whether the deposit buys anything. Handling: condition precedent before the March payment

Uncertainty: monthly peaks, launch clustering, molder holiday capacity uncommitted. Effect: fill-rate misses even when annual capacity fits. Handling: monthly simulation; 2027 safety stock; holiday capacity in the molder contract

Uncertainty: specialty: +2 months' validation; 4-point scrap allowance missing from forecast. Effect: line later and capacity ~0.1M units lower. Handling: allowance built in; 14-month line timeline; molder validation quote

Uncertainty: construction inflation; no salvage value; 2027-30 operating cash flow (not in pack). Effect: capex and cash tests could move. Handling: fixed-price re-quote at Gate 2; 13-week cash forecast
No single uncertainty overturns the recommendation; together they explain why the $4.2M must wait for evidence. Items marked 'not in pack' are open data gaps, not estimates
We ask the committee for four decisions in January, none of which commits the $4.2M balance

Decision 1: Approve the $0.6M slot deposit for March 2027, on one condition: written supplier terms allowing an order date of Q1 2028 or later and confirming the lead time. If refused, decline the slot

Decision 2: Decline the full line order and any public capacity announcement now. Instead, let Sales use the reserved slot and molder plan privately to turn nonbinding forecasts into signed minimums or prepayments
Decision 3: Authorize the 2028 overflow plan: contract molder for 0.6M units, signed by June 2027 with holiday capacity; capped 2027 safety stock; specialty validation quote

Decision 4: Adopt the three release triggers and the gate calendar: demand of 10.5M units or more signed, or a simulated breach; at least $3.5M committed funding; readiness confirmed. Target Q1 2028, last date Q3 2028
Total cash committed by these decisions: $0.6M, leaving $8.2M against the $7.0M floor. Owners are proposed (management to confirm)
Supplier terms (order date, lead time, price). Owner: Procurement / Ops. By: Feb 2027
Molder RFQ incl. holiday capacity. Owner: Operations. By: Jun 2027
Monthly fill-rate simulation. Owner: Operations. By: Q2 2027
Funding term sheet (at least $3.5M). Owner: CFO. By: Q4 2027
Signed-volume / prepayment talks. Owner: VP Sales. By: Ongoing
13-week cash forecast vs floor. Owner: Finance. By: Monthly
Specialty share in 2028 and 2030 (gap in the pack): 0% in 2028; 20% in 2030 (same as 2029). Effect if wrong: +/-0.1M units of overflow
Judgment calls made where the pack was silent; each is flagged so the committee can challenge it. These choices were made without access to management; the committee should confirm or replace them
Built only from the IC briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); no external research. Investment Committee pre-read, for decision at the January 2027 IC
